question: Down syndrome is caused by:
explanation:
• Down syndrome (trisomy 21): three copies of chromosome 21.
• Associated with intellectual disability, characteristic facies, cardiac defects.

question: Turner syndrome karyotype is:
explanation:
• Turner syndrome: 45, X (one X only). Female phenotype, short stature, ovarian failure.
• 47, XXY = Klinefelter.

question: Benign tumor characteristically:
explanation:
• Benign: well-differentiated, localized, no invasion or metastasis.
• Malignant: invasion, metastasis, poor differentiation.

question: Acute inflammation is characterized by:
explanation:
• Acute: neutrophils, vasodilation, edema, redness, heat, pain.
• Chronic: lymphocytes, macrophages, fibrosis.

question: Iron deficiency anemia shows:
options: D. No change in RBC size
explanation:
• Iron deficiency: microcytic, hypochromic anemia (low MCV, MCH).
• B12/folate deficiency: macrocytic.

question: Autosomal dominant inheritance means:
options: B. One copy of mutant gene can cause disease; 50% offspring risk
D. Both parents must carry gene
explanation:
• Autosomal dominant: one mutated copy sufficient; each child has 50% chance.
• E.g. Huntington disease, familial hypercholesterolemia.

question: Karyotype is used to:
options: B. Visualize chromosome number and structure
explanation:
• Karyotype: arrangement of chromosomes to detect numerical/structural abnormalities.
• Used in prenatal diagnosis and genetic disorders.

question: Tumor marker often associated with hepatocellular carcinoma:
explanation:
• AFP is elevated in hepatocellular carcinoma and some germ cell tumors.
• PSA for prostate; CA-125 for ovarian.

question: Hemophilia A is:
explanation:
• Hemophilia A (factor VIII deficiency) is X-linked recessive.
• Mainly affects males; females can be carriers.

question: Granuloma is typically seen in:
options: B. Tuberculosis and some fungal infections
explanation:
• Granuloma: collection of epithelioid macrophages (e.g. in TB, sarcoidosis, fungal).
• Type of chronic inflammation.

question: Klinefelter syndrome karyotype:
explanation:
• Klinefelter: 47, XXY. Male with tall stature, hypogonadism, infertility.
• Turner: 45, X.

question: Autosomal recessive: both parents carriers; risk for child:
explanation:
• Autosomal recessive: 25% affected, 50% carrier, 25% unaffected when both parents carriers.
• E.g. sickle cell, cystic fibrosis.

question: Malignant tumor characteristically:
explanation:
• Malignant: invasion, metastasis, anaplasia, rapid growth, recurrence.
• Benign: localized, no metastasis.

question: Chronic inflammation cell type predominates:
explanation:
• Chronic: lymphocytes, macrophages, plasma cells; fibrosis.
• Acute: neutrophils.

question: Megaloblastic anemia is due to deficiency of:
explanation:
• B12/folate deficiency: megaloblastic (large RBCs), macrocytic anemia.
• Iron deficiency: microcytic.

question: Biopsy is:
options: B. Removal of tissue for microscopic examination
explanation:
• Biopsy: tissue sample for histopathology (diagnosis of cancer, etc.).
• Fine needle, core, excisional.

question: X-linked recessive: affected males pass gene to:
options: B. All daughters (carriers); sons unaffected if mother not carrier
explanation:
• X-linked recessive: affected male → all daughters carriers; sons unaffected (father gives Y).
• Hemophilia, Duchenne.

question: Leukemia is:
options: B. Cancer of blood-forming cells (bone marrow, blood)
explanation:
• Leukemia: malignancy of hematopoietic cells; excess immature WBCs.
• Acute vs chronic; lymphoid vs myeloid.

question: Edema in inflammation is due to:
explanation:
• Acute inflammation: vasodilation, increased permeability → edema, redness, heat.
• Exudate leaks into tissue.

question: Sickle cell disease inheritance:
explanation:
• Sickle cell: autosomal recessive (HbS gene). Both copies needed for disease.
• Carrier (one copy) has sickle trait.
